title.title: The Correspondence of Esther Roberts Hunt Collins

msIdentifier.institution: Friends Historical Library of Swarthmore College

projectDesc.p: The correspondence of Quaker minister Esther Roberts Hunt Collins is stored at the Friends Historical Library of Swarthmore College. With the generous support of H. David and Joyce E. Hunt, Library staff scanned and transcribed these letters in 2024 and encoded the text in TEI.

div.p: I have very often felt an impulse, which I believe procedure from right the overflowing of the unfeigned love, to salute thee, my endeared Mother, with thee of the pen; but through a multiplicity of concerns which thou knowest are attendant on my station, letter writing is postponed from time to time as one of the non-essentials, until my faculty for that employ is become quite numb and almost useless for want of exercise. How striking a proof that it will not do to dig in the earth and bury our talents, however inconsiderable they may seem to us, for the wise & bounteous giver of all good is looking for fruits. And I feel a great jealousy for thy poor M, that her work is far behind and her capacity to labor in his vineyard rather weakened. Indeed I often feel so lost to every good that I am scarcely capable of breathing a sigh for my miserable self. I know not that there will be any use in my writing thus, but it came unsought for and I penned it without reflection, for writing to thee feels very similar to thinking aloud.

My dear E. had a letter from thee last week which we had thought very long in coming, not hearing from thee for a longer time than perhaps ever before. I observed it was silent with respect to coming next summer, but hope thou have it still in prospect. Our coming to Jersey was some time ago decided in the negative, for we could all no way for our being absent from home so long with propriety, and I suppose the decision was right, for if it had been otherwise we would probably have felt disappointed. Nearly three weeks ago I had my feet scalded with sugar water, and one of them still continue so bad that I know not whether it will be well before the time proposed for our going. This has been a very tedious, trying time of confinement, being a time when my service was more than usually needed; but I have endeavored to exercise all the patience I possess, believing that the wise dispenser of trials is able to sanctify them to us if we abide in the patience. I am now able to hop a little on one foot and can get into the kitchen without help, but for two weeks had to be helped there in the morning & back at night, for though I could do but little I conceived my presence there was needful.

Our neighbor Linn’s family has had a trying season of nursing. One of their sons has been very ill these two months, and several of the other children & mother have had turns of illness but recovered. I expect thou rememberest Sarah Betharm the young woman thou left us here; poor girl she was hurried out of time with a very short illness. I am not acquainted with the particulars, but she died at John Cock’s. Thy grandson Emmor is a fine, healthy boy, very large of his age and begins to require tuition. O dear Mother! Thou knowest the importance of a parents charge, and I know the unfitness of thy poor daughter to be exercised in it. He is not yet weaned from the breast but think it may be best to do it before the sickly season for children comes on. We are nearly through our winter’s spinning, say 30 yards of table linen, 20 yards of fine linen, 50 of shirting, & 30 of tow. Our Eva’s I think an improvising girl in business, she can spin her days work quite easily and she is very strong and able to do heavy work, & when needed can assist on the plantation. I have some thought of opening a school at home for this summer, but feel so many doubts respecting the propriety of it that I am as yet unable to determine. I think I am willing to be as helpful to my kind companion as possible.

closer.salute: Please to remember me affectionately to Sister R. I hope to see her this summer with thee & our dear Father, who I wish to be mentioned to from thy affectionate
